Use case: ui-mockup. Create OPTION A: a finished landscape mobile game SKILLS & INVENTORY reference screen. Input image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: faithfully match its fine detailed pixel fantasy art, gold carved borders, dark crimson lacquer, elegant ivory serif labels, moonlit Japanese castle atmosphere, bespoke restrained ornament. New screen, no main menu.
Design a usable symmetrical split screen: left 45% is a large full-body crimson-cloaked samurai in a stone shrine training courtyard, right 55% is a beautiful clear scrollable LIST of four illustrated skill cards. Top navigation INVENTORY | SKILLS, SKILLS selected; top right coin icon 1250, close X. Large header BLADE ARTS. Bottom subtle back button.
Left preview: character fully visible head to feet with generous room for effects, demonstrating selected ENERGY SLASH, an elegant crimson crescent leaving the katana and striking a small training target to the right of him. Fine sparks and faint ground ring, readable silhouette, no huge VFX hiding body. A small beautiful REPLAY button beneath character and PREVIEW label. This is a concept still depicting the future animated preview. Bottom left compact equipped sword and charm slots.
Right: clean roomy vertical rows with unique beautiful painted pixel skill icons, short readable titles and states: BLADE DISCIPLINE / OWNED; ENERGY SLASH / 300; TIDAL NOVA / 160; IRON HEART / 220. ENERGY SLASH row selected with restrained gold outline. At bottom right a selected-skill detail bar with icon, title ENERGY SLASH, one short line 'A ranged crimson blade.' and a large gold-rimmed BUY · 300 button. Skill selection and purchase are visibly separate controls. Coin balance remains 1250 during preview; no purchased message. Clear text, no dense stat clutter. Large touch targets, generous margins inside fine detailed screen frame.
Full bleed 16:9 screenshot, no physical phone, no outside annotations. Keep all controls legible and balanced. This must feel like a real premium game inventory with clear pixel-art character/equipment and highly detailed layered scenery. No generic flat dashboard, no photorealism, no modern sci-fi.
